 A $200,000 split equally across KO, CVX, MRK, and MCD generates $5,451 in annual passive income at a blended 2.73% yield. 
 McDonald's 16.96% year-to-date stock drop pushed its yield to 3.10%, the highest in the group, while its dividend remains covered 1.8x by adjusted EPS. 
 All four companies raised their quarterly payouts over the past year, so reinvesting dividends compounds the income stream without adding new capital. 
 Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor) 
 Once the paychecks stop, most retirees judge a portfolio by one number: how much cash shows up each quarter without selling a share. Blue-chip companies with long dividend records answer that question in up markets and down markets alike, because their payouts come from operating cash flow and not from the stock price. 
 Vitalii Vodolazskyi / Shutterstock.com Here's what a $50,000 investment in these four dividend names would produce. The total commitment is $200,000, and at forward yields, it produces more than $5,400 in annual passive income. All four pay quarterly, so the checks arrive on a predictable schedule. 
 Coca-Cola 
 Stock #4: Coca-Cola ( NYSE:KO ) 
 Forward Yield: 2.30% 
 Shares for $50,000: 541.95 
 Annual Passive Income: ~$1,148.93 
 Coca-Cola sells concentrate to bottling partners in more than 200 countries and territories. That capital-light model produced a 32.9% comparable operating margin in today's third-quarter results. Adjusted EPS of $0.91 beat the $0.88 estimate, and revenue rose 7.4% to $13.38 billion. 
 The yield is the lowest of the four because investors pay a premium for that stability. The stock trades at a P/E of 30 and has gained 34.54% year to date. On safety, management raised its 2026 free cash flow outlook to at least $13.0 billion, well above the about $9.1 billion the $2.12 annual dividend requires. Coca-Cola is a Dividend King with 60+ consecutive years of increases.

 Merck 
 Stock #3: Merck ( NYSE:MRK ) 
 Forward Yield: 2.43% 
 Shares for $50,000: 356.66 
 Annual Passive Income: ~$1,212.64 
 Merck develops medicines, vaccines, and animal health products. KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX brought in $8.37 billion in the second quarter, when total revenue rose 5.1% to $16.61 billion. The yield shows patent risk, since KEYTRUDA loses exclusivity late this decade. On the August call, chief executive Robert Davis called that period "more of a hill than a cliff." 
 Story Continues At first glance, the dividend looks stretched: 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $2.66 to $2.76 falls below the $3.40 annual payout. That guidance, however, includes one-time charges of $3.62 per share for Cidara and $2.31 per share for Terns. Adding those back, the dividend uses about 39% of underlying earnings. The quarterly rate rose to $0.85 from $0.81. One risk to keep an eye on: the shares fell after leaked cancer data disappointed investors on October 22. 
 Chevron 
 Stock #2: Chevron ( NYSE:CVX ) 
 Forward Yield: 3.08% 
 Shares for $50,000: 216.13 
 Annual Passive Income: ~$1,538.86 
 An integrated major, Chevron spans production, refining, and chemicals. The Hess acquisition raised worldwide output 20% to 4,070 MBOED. Energy stocks yield more because commodity swings make earnings volatile. That said, Chevron's yield has fallen as the stock climbed 56.01% year to date, with Brent at $104 versus $68 a year earlier. 
 Coverage is strong. Second-quarter free cash flow of $18.10 billion topped the about $13.96 billion the dividend costs over a full year. Chevron also cut debt by $8.41 billion and covers interest 13.7x. Wirth said Hess cash flow has been "roughly double the incremental dividends." The main exposure is oil prices, because affiliate distribution guidance assumes $70 Brent. 
 McDonald's 
 Stock #1: McDonald's ( NYSE:MCD ) 
 Forward Yield: 3.10% 
 Shares for $50,000: 200.87 
 Annual Passive Income: ~$1,550.70 
 Franchisees run about 95% of McDonald's 46,028 restaurants, so the company collects rent and royalties. Its year-to-date adjusted operating margin is 46.9%. McDonald's has the top yield in this group mostly because the stock has dropped 16.96% year-to-date while a squeezed consumer held global comparable sales growth to 1.3%. 
 The payout still looks well covered. Second-quarter adjusted EPS of $3.38 covered the $1.86 quarterly dividend about 1.8 times, and interest coverage is 7.8x. The board then raised the dividend to $1.93, payable December 15, 2026.

 Together, the four positions generate $5,451.13 in annual passive income on a $200,000 investment, a combined yield of 2.73%. McDonald's contributes $1,550.70, Chevron adds $1,538.86, Merck adds $1,212.64, and Coca-Cola rounds out the group with $1,148.93. 
 All four companies have raised their quarterly payouts over the past year, so income grows without adding new money. Reinvesting each quarterly check buys more shares, and those shares earn the next, larger dividend. Over a long holding period, that compounding is what turns a modest starting yield into a much bigger stream of retirement cash (we laid out the full mix, payout calendar, and withdrawal order for turning savings into a paycheck in a free guide here).
